LESSON: SURFACE AREA AND VOLUME OF SOLIDS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements and Geometry
Topic 2.7: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Surface Area and Volume of Solids, part of Measurements and Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we determine the surface area and volume of solids? 2. Why do we determine the surface area and volume of solids?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use models and nets of prisms, pyramids, cones, frustums, and spheres to calculate surface areas. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner support assistants or a scribe,

2. identify the components of a composite solid, calculate the surface area of each component and obtain the total surface area of the composite solid. Learners with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/sign/write), 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use models and nets of prisms, pyramids, cones, frustums, and spheres to calculate surface areas. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner support assistants or a scribe,
2. identify the components of a composite solid, calculate the surface area of each component and obtain the total surface area of the composite solid. Learners with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/sign/write), 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Surface Area and Volume of Solids together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving: as the learner uses a cylinder and a cone of the same radius and height, and

a substance such as sand or water, to determine the volume of a cone as a third of the volume of a cylinder.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner uses a cylinder and a cone of the same radius and height, and a substance

such as sand or water, to determine the volume of a cone as a third the volume of a cylinder.

Values:
● Unity: as the learner discusses in a group and establishes the relationship between the volume of a cone and the

volume of a cylinder.

● Respect: as the learner listens to others’ opinions as they discuss in groups and work out the volumes of prisms,

pyramids, cones, frustums and spheres.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environment and technology: as the learner collects and uses containers from the immediate environment and uses

them to discuss and work out their volumes.

55

Suggested Learning Resources

Geometrical instruments (padded compass, rulers with enhanced grip, protractor with handle), metre rule with handle,

mathematical tables, charts on multiplication tables/ solid objects, drawing/ manila papers, scissors with enhanced

grip, multipurpose communication boards on solid objects, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head pointers,

page turners, pen/pencil holders, adapted scientific calculators/ projectors, positioning devices such as special seats

with straps, adapted digital devices such as adapted computers with larger screens
